title: Returns-Servicing Surcharge on Paloma Business Subscriptions
content:
A monthly-billed Paloma Business account's subscription charge for a billing period carries a returns-servicing surcharge decided by the payouts that beneficiary banks returned in the six months before the day the charge is worked out, counted from the day after the same calendar day six months earlier up to and including that day. A payout counts when it has a return record dated inside the window.

### Surcharge ladder

| Payouts returned in the six-month window | Returns-servicing surcharge |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 15.00 USD |
| Exactly one | 6.00 USD |
| None | Nothing |

As a clause: two or more returned payouts add a returns-servicing surcharge of 15.00 USD; exactly one returned payout adds 6.00 USD; no returned payout adds nothing.

The surcharge is a fixed amount in US dollars added to the period's subscription charge. Every fixed amount the charge carries, deducted or added, acts at the same point, on the monthly fee as billed for the period after any percentage discount on that fee: the charge is that fee less every fixed amount deducted plus every fixed amount added, and only that result is held at no less than 0.00 and rounded half up to the cent.

### Examples (hypothetical)

- Charge worked out on 20 August: the window runs from 21 February through 20 August. One payout returned on 5 March, and no other in the window, adds 6.00 USD.
- Three payouts returned in the window add 15.00 USD, the same as two.
- A payout returned eight months before the charge is outside the window and adds nothing.
- A monthly fee as billed of 15.00 USD after any percentage discount, fixed deductions totalling 25.00 USD and a surcharge of 15.00 USD: 15.00 less 25.00 plus 15.00 gives 5.00 USD, the floor of 0.00 being tested only on that result.
